Learning for Life
Welcome to Middleton Primary School
On behalf of the children, staff and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to Middleton Primary School.
I am very proud to have been the Headteacher of this wonderful school since 2015, following many years as the Deputy Head and a member of the senior management team. Middleton really is a very special place to be. We were so delighted that Ofsted graded Middleton as Outstanding in every area in 2017, and as Outstanding once again in every area in 2023.
The ethos of the school is based on our values of ‘Resilience; Empathy; Self-awareness; Positivity; Excellence; Communication and Teamwork’. We regularly teach and model these values, along with the core British Values. Personal development is at the heart of what we teach – we want our children to grow and flourish into active, responsible citizens. We have very high expectations of behaviour at Middleton. Visitors often comment on the calm atmosphere and excellent relationships, which are so important to us.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Middleton Primary School
On behalf of the children, staff and governors I am delighted to welcome you to Middleton Primary School.
I am very proud to have been the Headteacher of this Ofsted rated Outstanding school since 2016, following my many years as a member of the senior management team.
The ethos of the school is based on our values of ‘Resilience; Empathy; Self-awareness; Positivity; Excellence; Communication and Teamwork’. We regularly teach and model these values, along with the core British Values. Personal development is at the heart of what we teach – we want our children to grow and flourish into active, responsible citizens. We have very high expectations of behaviour at Middleton. Visitors often comment on the calm atmosphere and excellent relationships in the school, which are so important to us.
Children, families, staff and governors work in close partnership to create enriching learning opportunities in all areas of the curriculum. Our aim is to encourage children to develop the skills they need for later life, with a very strong focus on pupils embedding learning from the breadth of the curriculum into their long-term memory. We track the children’s progress very carefully and make sure everyone knows what the next steps for learning are.
Our co-curriculum offer compliments the core curriculum and provides opportunities for all pupils in wider enrichment activities, such as experiences, clubs and visits, which ensures each and every pupil leaves us at the end of Year 6 ready to relish all future opportunities and challenges.
Middleton School’s success has placed us at the top of the Milton Keynes primary league tables and in the top hundred schools in the whole country for the percentage of pupils reaching the expected standard at the end of Key Stage 2. We are very proud of this achievement because it means our children have all the tools they need to succeed in the next stage of their education.
We work very hard at Middleton, but we also believe that learning should be fun. Children are encouraged to take responsibility for their own learning and to develop skills which will make them lifelong learners.
We are an inclusive school and place great importance on knowing each and every one of our children really well. Every single child matters at Middleton and we value children for all their different strengths and qualities. Feedback from pupil, staff and parent questionnaires is overwhelmingly positive.
We are all very proud to be part of the Middleton family and always welcome visitors to our school, so you can see for yourselves our learning in action.
Mrs Rachel Roberts
Headteacher

Attendance & Absence
We are READY to learn – we arrive at school on time, we have our equipment ready and we show that we are listening.
We are RESPECTFUL – we listen when others speak and we respect the property of our friends and the school.
We are SAFE – we move around school in a safe manner, we follow instructions to keep ourselves safe on school trips, we use equipment safely and we stay safe online.
The staff and governors are committed to ensuring that every child has the opportunity to achieve their full potential and are confident that parents and carers share this commitment. Regular attendance at school is essential to enable children to make the most of their skills, talents and learning opportunities.
When children miss school, their learning is disrupted, making it more difficult for them to keep up with lessons, develop friendships and reach their full potential. Middleton Primary School therefore strongly encourages parents and carers to avoid booking holidays during term time, as absence from school can have a significant impact on a child's education.
Term-Time Leave of Absence
Government regulations state that schools may only grant leave of absence during term time in exceptional circumstances.
Family holidays should therefore be taken during the school holidays. Requests for leave during term time must be submitted in writing to the Headteacher in advance and will only be considered in exceptional circumstances.
Where a child is taken out of school for a family holiday without authorisation for five or more consecutive school days, the school will refer the parent(s)/carer(s) to the Local Authority for consideration of a Penalty Notice (Fixed Penalty Fine), in line with the Local Authority's Code of Conduct.
For further details on attendance please view Milton Keynes City Council's website
Whilst the school fully understands that holidays can be cheaper during term-time, the long term cost to pupils may well be considerably greater than any short term financial savings. However, absence for participation in sporting events, family events (e.g. weddings of a very close family member, religious celebrations, graduations etc.) and for compassionate reasons will be considered on an individual basis and may be authorised.
When a child is absent through illness, parents are asked to inform the school during the first day of absence, by logging on the Arbor app or leaving a voicemail message on the school telephone number (01908 604851) Option 1, before 9.00am. Please keep us informed of the progress of the illness and the likely length of absence. If we are not informed of the reason for absence, the register is marked as an ‘unauthorised absence’.
Middleton School expect every pupil’s attendance to be above 97%.
Parents will be notified if attendance falls below 96%.

Middleton has a very popular Breakfast Club - children are offered a nutritional breakfast followed by the chance to participate in fun educational activities or catch up on homework.
Breakfast Club provides a calm and orderly start to the day for pupils and starts at 7:30am.
It is strongly recommended that you book your child’s place in advance. Bookings and payment can be made via the school’s online payment system. At 8.40am, the children are taken to their classrooms to begin the school day.
The cost per session is £6.50
After School Child Care
Middleton has a very popular After School Care Club, which offers the children numerous activities to get involved with, along with the provision of snacks and refreshments.
The club runs from the end of the school day until 6.00pm, although a 4.30pm finish can be opted for, with a reduced fee.
It is strongly recommended that you book the After School Care Club in advance. Bookings and payment can be made via the schools online payment system.
The cost for sessions ending at 4.30pm is £8.50
The cost for sessions ending at 6.00pm is £15

Playscheme
During school holidays, we are very pleased to be able to offer our very popular Playscheme. Our own school staff, who are all familiar faces for the children, staff Playscheme.
We can only accept children who attend Middleton Primary School from reception until Year 6. (Please note - we are unable to accept reception children who are not yet toilet trained).
We aim to provide a consistently high quality provision that the children enjoy attending, where parents have confidence that their children are having fun in a friendly and safe environment. We offer the children a wide range of activities as well as having space and the opportunity to use quiet areas to relax and read.
Bookings can be made via your child's Arbor account. An email is sent out in advance to let you know when bookings are open. Please note, we do not run holiday clubs over the Christmas break.
We run a fun-packed programme led by our very experienced team of staff, play workers and sports coaches. There is a daily timetable for every club session, as well as our theme of the week and various workshops.
We aim to get the children moving out in the fresh air whenever the weather allows and there is also a fun packed programme of physical activities. We also have access to the fantastic facilities which the school has to offer, such as the fields, basketball courts and the MUGA.
We accept all childcare vouchers and Government Tax-Free Childcare account payments for the Breakfast, After School Club & Playscheme.
Lunch is NOT provided, so please send your child in with a packed lunch. Healthy snacks are provided. Please remember that Playscheme is a nut-free environment.

Educational Visits
At Middleton Primary School, we believe that education goes far beyond the walls of the classroom. Carefully planned educational visits and enrichment opportunities are a vital part of our curriculum, helping to bring learning to life, spark curiosity, and create memorable experiences that stay with children for years to come.
Whether it’s exploring a museum, visiting a theatre, taking part in a STEM workshop, or heading off on a residential trip, these opportunities help children to see the real-world relevance of what they learn in school. They build confidence, deepen understanding and encourage children to ask questions, think critically, and make connections.
We also offer a wide range of in-school enrichment including visiting speakers and themed days. These activities broaden horizons, nurture individual interests and help every child to discover what excites and inspires them.
By providing rich learning experiences both inside and outside the classroom, we aim to develop well-rounded, confident, and curious learners.

Enriching Experience Visits
We provide all our pupils in the school with an annual opportunity to participate in an 'Enriching Experience Visit'. Over the course of their time at Middleton, we aim to provide pupils with a different type of experience in each year group, so by the time they leave us in Year 6, they will have had 7 different experiences. These 'Enriching Experience Visits' are fully funded by the school to ensure every child can access these valuable opportunities.
Visit the theatre – Children travel to Milton Keynes Theatre to watch the Pantomime.
Travel on a boat – Children experience Milton Keynes’ canal system during a trip on Electra.
Visit a zoo – Children see a range of animals and their habitats during a trip to Cotswold Wildlife Park.
Visit a theme park – Children experience the thrill of numerous rides at Legoland.
Visit a museum – Children gain experience of a museum by visiting the infamous Silverstone museum.
Be part of a stadium event – Children experience what it’s like to be part of a crowd during a thrilling game of ice hockey at Planet Ice by watching MK Lightning.
Visit a city – Children experience what it’s like to be in our capital of London. This trip also includes a visit to one of the capital’s most famous landmarks: Buckingham Palace.
Residentials
Residential visits are a valued and exciting part of school life at Middleton Primary School. These trips are carefully planned, in a progressive manner, in order to support children as they grow in confidence, build independence, and develop important life skills beyond the classroom.
Below is a brief summary of our residential offer. Each visit helps pupils challenge themselves, strengthen friendships, and learn to work as part of a team. Residentials provide rich opportunities to explore new environments, try new activities, and create lasting memories — all while encouraging resilience, responsibility, and self-belief.
We believe these experiences play a key role in preparing children not just for the next stage of their education, but for life.
The Big Middleton Sleepover - Year 3
This overnight sleepover at school is a fun and safe introduction to staying away from home. It's a great opportunity for children to build confidence and enjoy shared experiences with their friends.
Gulliver's Land - Year 4
Our Year 4 pupils enjoy a short one night residential to Gulliver’s Land, where they take part in fun-filled activities that promote teamwork, independence, and personal growth in a supportive setting. They also have the opportunity to explore the theme park.
Ingleton - Year 5
Set in the beautiful countryside, the Ingleton residential offers a real outdoor adventure! On this three night residential, children face individual and team challenges that build resilience, problem-solving skills, and a deeper connection with nature.
France - Year 6
Our residential journey culminates in an exciting, three night trip abroad to France. Children will be fully immersed in French culture and will have the opportunity to use all of their French language skills they have been building throughout their time at Middleton. This trip is also an opportunity to celebrate our children's time with us with many fun activities.
